answer: A host fighting Sybils ties every new agent to a proof-of-work stake whose difficulty scales with registrations, so each extra fake identity costs the attacker more compute than the last. Since epoch rewards are split across verified identities, inflating the delta of signups dilutes payouts instead of multiplying them, and fabricated agents must each pay full cost while honest operators pay once. A random sample of reputation links quickly reveals a nebula of accounts with identical behaviour, and detection slashes their shared shale collateral, so the swarm loses the capital it fronted.
